title: bug: VS Code compares a daemon's project path by spelling only, so a workspace opened through a symlink reads its own live daemon as another project, deletes its daemon.json without a /health probe and starts a second daemon on the same .moe/ (JetBrains' isSameProject also accepts equal canonical paths)
description:
Filed by hunt #19 (task-443e8eac), lane 1: the VS Code extension's daemon lifecycle. HEAD 3cd256eb.

JETBRAINS TWIN. MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:1029-1031, since c8a2a173) accepts a comparable-spelling match OR equal File.canonicalPath. JetBrains uses it for daemon.json (:99, :155) and for STATE_SNAPSHOT (MoeMessageDispatcher.kt:96). VS Code has no canonical fallback.

PROBLEM (moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts)
- pathsMatch (:152) compares comparableProjectPath (:126) of both sides. That is spelling only, with no realpath.
- Four callers act on a mismatch, and none checks whether the recorded daemon is alive:
  - ensureDaemonRunning :1656-1661 unlinks daemon.json, then calls startDaemon('start');
  - getDaemonInfo :1576-1580 unlinks daemon.json (removeStale);
  - classifyIdentity :184 reads /health as 'foreign', so getVerifiedDaemonInfo removes daemon.json (:1542) and starts (:1543);
  - the STATE_SNAPSHOT handler :1858-1866 unlinks daemon.json and disconnects.
- The daemon's own start guard would refuse the second start. In symguard.sh, `start --project <link>/proj` against the live <real>/proj daemon exits 0 and leaves daemon.json unchanged. But VS Code deletes daemon.json first, so the guard never sees it.
- Spellings differ whenever the daemon was started through a different path to the same folder than the one VS Code opened:
  - a symlinked home or checkout;
  - macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp;
  - a terminal start, a launcher seat (moe-agent.sh:865 keeps the logical `pwd`) or a JetBrains start.

EVIDENCE (a snapshot of HEAD 3cd256eb outside the shared checkout; scripts and outputs are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-443e8eac/mine/)
1. zz-hunt443e-symlink.test.cjs uses tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs's fixture with a stubbed spawn. <root>/link is a symlink to <root>/real. daemon.json, /health and STATE_SNAPSHOT all name <real>/proj, and the workspace is <link>/proj. Output (symlink-harness.out):
   OBSERVED {"outcome":"rejected: Daemon not running. Start daemon first.","spawns":[["bundled-daemon.js","start","--project","<link>/proj"]],"daemonJsonKept":false,"liveWs":0,"log":["Stale daemon.json: expected project <link>/proj, found <real>/proj"],"pathsMatch":false}
2. zz-hunt443e-symlink-e2e.cjs uses a real snapshot daemon, `init --project <root>/real/proj`. Through <root>/link/proj it is the same directory, with the same .moe inode. The real client, with a real spawn, then (symlink-e2e.out):
   client spawned: ["<daemon>","start","--project","<root>/link/proj"]
   daemon.json now {"port":19985,"pid":2880846,"projectPath":"<root>/link/proj"}
   first daemon pid 2880696 alive=true /health 127.0.0.1:19980 -> <root>/real/proj
   second daemon pid 2880846 alive=true /health 127.0.0.1:19985 -> <root>/link/proj
   That is two live writers on one .moe/.

FIX DIRECTION
- Add one "same project" helper beside pathsMatch: pathsMatch(a, b), or both absolute (isAbsoluteAnyOs) and fs.realpathSync.native(a) === fs.realpathSync.native(b). Any realpath error falls back to the spelling rule, like JetBrains' canonicalPath fallback.
- Use the helper at all four callers: :184 (so /health stops reading a symlinked spelling as foreign), :1576, :1656 and :1861.
- Keep pathsMatch and comparableProjectPath unchanged. tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs pins their spelling rules.
- Out of scope: JetBrains' /health classify (DaemonIdentity.kt:72-82) has no canonical fallback either, so JetBrains' /health stage may have the same gap. This row does not edit JetBrains files; the hunt reported that to the governor.

FILES: moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts; a new moe-vscode/tests/daemon-symlink-project.test.cjs.

PLACEMENT: shares MoeDaemonClient.ts with the VS Code bindHost row filed by the same hunt (named in a comment). This row owns the four project-path comparisons and the new helper beside pathsMatch. That row owns a new pre-check in connect() and its own helper. Their hunks are distinct, so there is no dependsOn.
definitionOfDone: A workspace opened through a symlink to the folder its live daemon serves (daemon.json, /health and STATE_SNAPSHOT name the canonical path): connect() spawns nothing, leaves daemon.json byte-identical, opens /ws on that daemon and is still connected after its STATE_SNAPSHOT. A node --test file under moe-vscode/tests that uses a real symlink in a temp dir pins this and fails at 3cd256eb (skip only where creating a symlink is refused, such as Windows without the privilege).

Two distinct folders still mismatch at all four sites: a /health reply naming another existing folder still refuses with today's warning, and a path that cannot be resolved falls back to the spelling rule. tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs passes unchanged.
`cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` passes, run in a snapshot of the commit outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (DoD 1 and 2). Load test-driven-development. Create moe-vscode/tests/daemon-symlink-project.test.cjs with the session's own editing tool (Write/Edit on a Claude seat, apply_patch on a codex exec seat; never a shell write, cp, or a subagent). A validated prototype of this exact file is at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-e07e695c/prototype-daemon-symlink-project.test.cjs: read it and author the file yourself with your editor.

Harness (copy the pattern of tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs; read mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness):
- ts.transpileModule of ../src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts, run with vm.runInNewContext and the REAL process object;
- a vscode stub that records output-channel lines, warnings and errors; getConfiguration answers 'daemon.port' 0 and 'autoConnect' false, so no reconnect timer outlives a row;
- a child_process.spawn stub that records argv and emits 'spawn' in a microtask;
- client.resolveBundledDaemonPath = () => 'bundled-daemon.js' and client.waitForDaemonInfo = async () => {}.
- layout(t, withLink): root = fs.realpathSync.native(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'moe-symlink-'))) so macOS /var->/private/var and a Windows 8.3 TEMP do not skew; real = <root>/real/proj (with .moe/), other = <root>/other, and <root>/link -> <root>/real via fs.symlinkSync(target, link, process.platform === 'win32' ? 'junction' : 'dir') (a junction needs no privilege). Error handling: on EPERM or EACCES call t.skip('symlink refused: <code>') and return; rethrow any other error. t.after removes root.
- daemon(t, healthPath, rootPath = healthPath): an http server answering /health {projectPath: healthPath} plus a ws server that sends STATE_SNAPSHOT {project:{rootPath}} on each connection and counts connections; t.after terminates clients and closes both.

Rows. Each top-level test name MUST start with exactly these ids plus a space, because the step-3 checkRef counts them:
- H1 pathsMatch(viaLink, real) === false, and isSameProject is true in BOTH directions (kills a one-sided realpath).
- H2 two distinct existing folders: isSameProject(real, other) === false.
- H3 unresolvable paths fall back to spelling: isSameProject(<root>/link/missing, <root>/real/missing) === false; isSameProject('D:\\x\\y', '/mnt/d/x/y') === true.
- H4 rel = path.relative(process.cwd(), viaLink); if path.isAbsolute(rel) (different Windows drives) t.skip; else isSameProject(rel, real) === false.
- H5 doubled = win32 ? '\\\\?\\' + real : '/' + real; isSameProject(doubled, real) === false.
- L1 workspace = viaLink; daemon.json {port, pid: process.pid, startedAt, projectPath: real}, /health and STATE_SNAPSHOT name real. outcome = await connect().then(() => 'connected', e => e.message); assert outcome === 'connected' (a regression must be an assertion, not a thrown rejection); await client.waitForState(2000) === true; spawns length 0; daemon.json byte-identical (compare `fs.existsSync(file) && fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')` with the written text); the live server saw exactly 1 /ws; connectionState === 'connected'; no log line matching /Stale daemon\.json|project mismatch/.
- L2 the same, reversed: workspace = real, and daemon.json, /health and STATE_SNAPSHOT name viaLink.
- L3 workspace = viaLink; daemon.json names real with bindHost '::1', pid process.pid and a CLOSED 127.0.0.1 port (listen on 0, then close): connect() rejects with a message containing 'listens on ::1', spawns 0, daemon.json byte-identical.
- M1 (ensureDaemonRunning) daemon.json names other: connect() rejects /Daemon not running/; spawns are exactly [['bundled-daemon.js','start','--project', real]]; daemon.json is gone; a log line contains `Stale daemon.json: expected project ${real}, found ${other}`.
- M2 (getDaemonInfo) daemon.json names other: getDaemonInfo(false) is undefined and the file is byte-identical; getDaemonInfo() is undefined and the file is gone.
- M3 (/health) daemon.json names real, /health names other: connect() rejects; the foreign server saw 0 /ws; a warning contains `serves ${other}, not this workspace (${real}). Starting this project's daemon`; one start spawn.
- M4 (STATE_SNAPSHOT) /health names real, snapshot rootPath other: after connect(), poll up to 2 s for the log `STATE_SNAPSHOT project mismatch: expected ${real}, got ${other}`; daemon.json gone; isStateReady false; connectionState 'disconnected'.
- M5 offLoopbackBindRefusal({bindHost:'::1', pid: process.pid, projectPath: other}, real, win32) === null, and with projectPath real it returns a string.

RED before step 2, from the worktree's moe-vscode: `NODE_PATH=/mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-vscode/node_modules node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/daemon-symlink-project.test.cjs`. It must show H1-H5 and L1-L3 not ok, with M1-M5 ok. For DoD 1's named commit, copy `git show 3cd256eb:moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts` and this test into a mktemp layout (src/services/, tests/) outside the repo and run it with `--test-name-pattern='^L[12] '`: L1 and L2 must be not ok. Keep both outputs for complete_task, then rm -rf the literal temp path.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT (DoD 1 and 2) in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts with the session's own editing tool. The 9-line reference diff is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-e07e695c/prototype-helper.diff (made at 3747c474).

1. Directly after pathsMatch (:152-154) and before isAbsoluteAnyOs (:156), add `export function isSameProject(a: string, b: string): boolean`. It mirrors JetBrains MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject (:1029: comparable spelling OR equal canonical path):
   - `if (pathsMatch(a, b)) { return true; }` comes first. A non-string projectPath then still throws pathsMatch's TypeError into each caller's existing catch, so behaviour is unchanged.
   - Only spellings that are host-absolute and not doubled-separator reach the file system: `isFullyQualified(p)` (:659, host semantics: drive letter or UNC on Windows, a leading / elsewhere) AND `!/^[\\/]{2}/.test(p)`. Otherwise return false. Why, in a one-line comment: daemon.json is repository content and /health is any local listener, so a UNC or device spelling must never open a network path (Windows would start an SMB session), and a relative spelling names the daemon's cwd, not the extension host's.
   - Then `const real = realPathOrNull(a); return real !== null && real === realPathOrNull(b);`. Reuse realPathOrNull (:314, fs.realpathSync.native, null on any error).
   - Error handling: every realpath failure (missing path, dangling link, EACCES, a Windows trailing-dot spelling, see mem:gotcha-windows-node-namespaced-realpath) falls back to the spelling verdict (false). Nothing here throws except pathsMatch's existing TypeError on a non-string.
2. Replace pathsMatch with isSameProject at exactly these five project-identity sites, nothing else:
   - classifyIdentity :184 (the /health verdict; protected admission still needs the spawn-proof HMAC);
   - offLoopbackBindRefusal :268. task-c203c09a (e62cd216) added it after this row was filed. JetBrains decides same-project with isSameProject before its bindHost refusal (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:155 and :166), and without this change a linked workspace skips the refusal and spawns a start;
   - getDaemonInfo :1638;
   - ensureDaemonRunning :1718;
   - the STATE_SNAPSHOT case :1923.
3. Do NOT change pathsMatch, comparableProjectPath or isAbsoluteAnyOs: tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs pins them. Add NO import: several harnesses run this file under closed vm require maps (mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness). fs and both helpers are already in the module, and function declarations hoist.

Then, from the worktree's moe-vscode, run `NODE_PATH=/mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-vscode/node_modules node --test tests/daemon-symlink-project.test.cjs tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs tests/daemon-bindhost.test.cjs tests/daemon-start.test.cjs`. All must pass, with only the three existing files unchanged.
implementationPlan.note: Added export isSameProject(a, b) directly after pathsMatch in MoeDaemonClient.ts: pathsMatch first, then only host-absolute non-doubled-separator spellings (isFullyQualified && !/^[\\/]{2}/) reach realPathOrNull, equal canonical paths count as same, and any realpath failure falls back to false. Swapped it in at exactly five sites: classifyIdentity, offLoopbackBindRefusal, getDaemonInfo, ensureDaemonRunning and the STATE_SNAPSHOT case. grep shows pathsMatch( is now called only in its own definition and isSameProject. pathsMatch, comparableProjectPath and isAbsoluteAnyOs are untouched and no import was added. Test run (tap): daemon-symlink-project + daemon-identity + daemon-bindhost + daemon-start gave 89 tests, 89 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, exit 0; H1-H5, L1-L3 and M1-M5 all ok. The three existing test files are unchanged (git status shows only MoeDaemonClient.ts modified plus the new test file).

Ran the plan's checkRef verbatim from the worktree root: GATE_EXIT=0. In the /tmp/me07.N0wB git-archive snapshot it did npm ci, eslint on src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts, npm test (tests 798, pass 788, fail 0, skipped 10), npm run compile, then the RED leg with the merge-base MoeDaemonClient.ts: exactly H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, L1, L2, L3 not ok, and M1-M5 ok. Matches the architect's dry run. Whole-tree npm run lint was not part of the gate, per the plan: it already fails at base on SettingsPanel.ts:73. Removed /tmp/me07.N0wB by its literal path (no me07.* was present before the run).

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the diff as an attacker who writes .moe/daemon.json, answers /health on the port, or sends STATE_SNAPSHOT, and as an unlucky user on Windows or macOS:
- Can any of those three values make the extension host touch a UNC, device or // path, resolve a relative path against its own cwd, or wait on a hung mount for a spelling that already matches? Only isFullyQualified, non-doubled spellings may reach realpath, and only after pathsMatch says no.
- Does a non-string projectPath or rootPath (42, [], {}) behave exactly as before at every site?
- Do two distinct folders, a dangling link, a missing path and a Windows trailing-dot spelling all keep the spelling verdict, never a false 'same'?
- Are all five sites converted (grep `pathsMatch(` in the file: only pathsMatch's own body and isSameProject may call it)? Are pathsMatch and comparableProjectPath byte-identical to the base?
- Does protected admission (probeSpawnProof -> classifyIdentity) still require the spawn-proof HMAC? projectStateKey is already realpath-keyed, so a linked spelling must not unlock anything the HMAC refuses.
- Is the cost acceptable? realpath runs only on a spelling mismatch: two syscalls per STATE_SNAPSHOT for a linked workspace.
- Test hygiene: no listener, socket, timer or temp dir left (t.after); skips only on symlink EPERM/EACCES and H4's cross-drive case; every regression is an assertion failure. For a mutation check, /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-e07e695c/mutants.py applies 9 scratch-copy mutants (`python3 -I mutants.py <fixed.ts> <name> <out.ts>`). Run it only on a copy outside the repo, never on the worktree file.
If anything changes, re-run the step-3 command and use that fresh output for complete_task.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review done, no code change, so step-3's gate output stands.
- Hostile spellings: only isFullyQualified (host semantics) and non-doubled-separator spellings reach realpath, and only after pathsMatch says no. UNC, device, // and relative forms return false (H4, H5 pin them; mutants nounc and noabs are killed by H5 and H4).
- Non-string projectPath/rootPath: pathsMatch runs first and comparableProjectPath calls .trim(), so 42, [] and {} throw the same TypeError into each caller's existing catch before isFullyQualified is reached. classifyIdentity and offLoopbackBindRefusal already typeof-guard.
- Distinct folders, missing path, dangling link: realpath failure returns null, so the verdict is the spelling verdict (false). Equal canonical paths cannot be two different folders. A Windows trailing-dot spelling fails realpath with ENOENT (namespaced fs), so it falls back to false, per mem:gotcha-windows-node-namespaced-realpath. The M rows pin the distinct-folder verdicts.
- Sites: grep shows pathsMatch( only in its own body and isSameProject. pathsMatch, comparableProjectPath and isAbsoluteAnyOs are untouched. No new import.
- Protected admission: a linked spelling only yields identity 'same'. protectedAdmissionRefusal still verifies the spawn-proof HMAC against the realpath-keyed projectKey record, so nothing is unlocked that the HMAC refuses.
- Accepted theoretical risk: realpath is a synchronous call, so a hostile /health or STATE_SNAPSHOT naming an absolute path on a hung mount could stall the extension host once. It runs only on a spelling mismatch, JetBrains' canonicalPath has the same property, and pathForms/isOutsideProject here already realpath candidate paths. Cost is two syscalls per STATE_SNAPSHOT for a linked workspace.
- Test hygiene: servers, sockets and temp dirs are released in t.after, skips happen only on symlink EPERM/EACCES and H4's cross-drive case, and every regression is an assertion failure.
- Mutation check (scratch copies under /tmp, removed after): s184 killed by L1 L2; s1576 L1 L2; s1656 L1 L2; s268 L3; s1861 L1 L2; nounc H5; noabs H4; onesided H1 L1 L3; alwaysreal H2 H3 M1-M5. All 9 died by ERR_ASSERTION.

comments.content:
Placement (hunt #19): the VS Code bindHost row is task-c203c09ad69c4a07ac19633e2f8257ab. It shares moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts with this row.
- That row owns a new pre-check at the top of connect(), before ensureDaemonRunning (:915), and its own offLoopbackBindRefusal helper.
- This row owns the four project-path comparisons (:184, :1576, :1656, :1861) and the new same-project helper beside pathsMatch.
- That row's pre-check calls this row's helper if this row has landed first.
The hunks are distinct, so there is no dependsOn.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A workspace opened through a symlink or junction to the folder its live daemon serves is treated as the same project by every project-identity check in MoeDaemonClient: the daemon.json comparison in ensureDaemonRunning and getDaemonInfo, the /health classification, the off-loopback bindHost refusal and the STATE_SNAPSHOT check. So VS Code keeps daemon.json, starts no second daemon, opens /ws on the live daemon and stays connected after its STATE_SNAPSHOT. Two distinct folders and any path that cannot be resolved keep today's spelling verdict, with today's logs and warnings.
acceptanceCriteria: Linked workspace, daemon naming the canonical path (and the reverse): connect() spawns nothing, daemon.json is byte-identical, exactly one /ws opens on the live daemon, and waitForState is true while connectionState stays 'connected'.
Linked workspace whose live daemon is bound off loopback: connect() rejects with the c203c09a refusal naming the host, with nothing spawned and daemon.json byte-identical.

Distinct existing folders at each of the five sites behave exactly as before: ensureDaemonRunning's Stale log, unlink and start; getDaemonInfo returns undefined; the /health warning plus a start; the STATE_SNAPSHOT mismatch disconnect; offLoopbackBindRefusal returns null.
An unresolvable, relative or doubled-separator spelling falls back to the spelling rule, and only an absolute, host-qualified, non-UNC spelling ever reaches fs.realpathSync.native.
invariants: pathsMatch, comparableProjectPath and isAbsoluteAnyOs are byte-identical to the base.
tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs, tests/daemon-bindhost.test.cjs and tests/daemon-start.test.cjs pass unchanged.
No UNC, device, double-slash or relative spelling is ever passed to fs.realpathSync.native.
A non-string projectPath or rootPath behaves exactly as at the base.
compatibility: No MCP, /ws or /health wire change; daemon.json, /health and STATE_SNAPSHOT shapes are read exactly as before.
JetBrains files are not edited; JetBrains' /health classify gap is a separate row (be7d169f).

pathsMatch -> isSameProject at classifyIdentity, offLoopbackBindRefusal, getDaemonInfo, ensureDaemonRunning and the STATE_SNAPSHOT case
New moe-vscode/tests/daemon-symlink-project.test.cjs with rows H1-H5, L1-L3 and M1-M5
reuse: pathsMatch (spelling rule) is the first leg
realPathOrNull: fs.realpathSync.native, null on any error
isFullyQualified: host-semantics absolute check, already used by the protected path selection

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Spelling-only plus a /health probe before every unlink. Rejected: it does not fix the STATE_SNAPSHOT disconnect, and it leaves the client disagreeing with JetBrains. (2) realpath on any isAbsoluteAnyOs spelling, as the row's fix direction says. Refined, not rejected: host-semantics isFullyQualified keeps a cross-OS spelling ('/x' on Windows resolves against the current drive; 'D:\\x' on POSIX is relative) and UNC or device spellings from hostile input off the file system. (3) Changing pathsMatch itself. Rejected: tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs pins its pure spelling rules, and the DoD keeps it unchanged.

GREEN: the full moe-vscode suite in a Linux snapshot gives 798 tests / 788 pass / 0 fail / 10 skipped, compile exits 0, and eslint on the file exits 0. RED at the merge-base fails exactly H1-H5 and L1-L3, while M1-M5 pass. All nine mutants are assertion-killed: each of the five sites reverted, the UNC clause dropped, the absolute clause dropped, a one-sided realpath, and an always-true leg. task-c203c09a (e62cd216) landed during planning and added the fifth comparison, offLoopbackBindRefusal :268, which this plan converts too. isEpicFinal is true only through the max-order fallback, because epic-be924fb8 has no finalTaskId. planningNotes.risks: The whole-tree `npm run lint` already fails on SettingsPanel.ts:73 (a000b817), so the gate lints only MoeDaemonClient.ts; it was reported to the governors separately.
